text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Foreign minister Granic, speaking in New York, said the United Nations mandate in Eastern Slavonia should end as planned.
- Workers of the ailing state-owned Sibenik HRM shipyard announce protests as their company gets formal praises but no jobs.
- Dalmatian hoteliers unable to pay debts to the Bank for reconstruction and development as financial results are still far from the prewar ones.
- Chamber of economy says surplus value tax is an elegant solution for the present tax system.
- Croatia excpects tourism to yield $1.3 billion this year, central bank's governor says.
- Minister of economy pressured state-owned oil company INA to lower prices to preserve social stability.
- Many companies give incentives to executives, but only rare ones like Pliva, Kras and Zagrebacka Banka keep it public.
- General manager of food processor Podravka says small share-holders to own 47 percent of the company if Privatisation fund reduces its share of the basic capital.
- Economic institute says production increased by 2.3 in this years first eight months.
- German Global Sourcing and former general manger Antic made offers below nominal value to privatise once most sucessful Zadar's company for special tool machines SAS.
- Return of Croatian emigration and tehir capital is slowed down by those who like to buy without paying, head of Croatian Association of hoteliers in Germany, Sime Ivancevic says.
- Euphoric growth of all shares registered on Croatian market last week, confectioner Kras fared best. -- Zgareb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
